correctness.rationale: For the periodically forced high-density predator-free logistic equation, inward pointing vector fields at u,v and strictly negative fprime over u>K/2 make the time-T map a contraction and produce a unique attracting periodic x_s in that interval. Nonconstant mean-zero forcing ensures variance V>0. Averaging the quadratic logistic equation gives exact V=delta(Delta-delta), delta=Xplus-mean(x_s) in (0,Delta/2), hence delta=(Delta-sqrt(Delta²-4V))/2>V/Delta. The supporting-line inequality for convex negative-slope p and concave positive-slope p gives opposite strictly signed C(avg p(x_s)-p(Xplus)) shifts with claimed sharp symbolic variance expression. Triangular predator-free variational system has multipliers exp(int fprime) and exp(T(C avg p-d)), proving actual transverse stability reversal for d strictly between thresholds. Independently verified rational trapping margins f(u)-h0=9/200, h0-f(v)=11/200, group response p(3/2)=90/19, pprime=-2400/361 and curvature sign, ordinary response 9/13, 48/169 and opposite curvature. Numerical waveforms are not needed for all-waveform proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The seasonal-harvesting bifurcation and invariant-torus results are about positive coexistence or perturbative periodic orbits; they do not dominate this waveform-uniform convexity/variance comparison on high-density predator-free cycles. Jensen inequalities are broader but require the exact mean displacement proved using forced logistic conservation, so do not by themselves imply the stated threshold bounds.

originality.rationale: An unusually relevant primary source, Chen/Huang/Ruan/Wang (2013) on seasonal prey harvesting and predator-prey invariant tori, was inspected in open full text, particularly model setup and Section 4. It analyzes a different seasonal bifurcation/coexistence regime and does not give the exact high-density predator-free Floquet threshold shift for *every* zero-mean waveform. Prior constant-harvest generalized Gause/group-defense threshold work has no forcing. Resultary discovered related mean-variance shells in other predator-prey models but not this same signed local invasion comparison. Classical Jensen and Floquet tools alone are not the identical prior theorem.
residual_risks: An unindexed periodic-harvest invasion theorem using exactly the same Jensen and mean-variance argument may predate this result.
Strict assumptions exclude large forcing, saddle lower prey branch, mixed-curvature responses and predator coexistence.
The three numerical waveforms in source are corroborative; the arbitrary-period/waveform result relies solely on contraction and averaged identities.

value.rationale: The arbitrary-period, arbitrary-waveform finite-amplitude signed stability-reversal theorem answers a natural ecological invasion question in a group-defense versus monotone-saturation model without relying on an asymptotic forcing regime. Exact variance-controlled quantitative thresholds and the possibility of opposite predator-invasion classifications at identical average harvest are independently useful, beyond simply renaming Jensen. Scope explicitly excludes global predator persistence.
